Ashford's population increased by around 14,800 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 130,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Ashford increased by 12.5%, from just under 118,000 in 2011 to around 132,700 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the South East (7.5%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Ashford was home to around 1.6 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 1.5 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 25% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Ashford than across the South East

Median age in Ashford

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Ashford increased by one year, from 40 to 41 years of age.

This area had a similar average (median) age to the South East as a whole in 2021 (41 years) but a slightly higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 4,800 (an increase of 21.9%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just over 1,200 (4.8% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.5 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Ashford residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 112,500 Ashford residents said they were born in England. This represented 84.7% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 104,400 in 2011, which at the time represented 88.5% of Ashford's population.

Southern Asian countries (other than Afghanistan, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka) were the next most represented, with around 3,300 Ashford residents reporting one of these countries as their country of birth (2.5%). This figure was up from around 1,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.1% of the population of Ashford.

The number of Ashford residents born in Scotland fell from around 1,400 in 2011 (1.2% of the local population) to around 1,300 in 2021 (1.0%).

In 2021, 84.7% of Ashford residents reported their country of birth as England

Rise in private renting

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in Ashford (3.4 percentage points) than in nearby Folkestone and Hythe (0.3 percentage points).

In Ashford, the percentage of private renting increased from 14.3% in 2011 to 17.7% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Folkestone and Hythe increased from 22.2% to 22.5%.

The rate of social renting in Ashford fell from 14.5% to 14.0%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 68.4% to 66.4%.

Private renting in Ashford increased by 3.4 percentage points

Unpaid care in Ashford

In 2021, 4.4% of Ashford residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.1% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.8%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.3% in 2011. The proportion of Ashford residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 2.6% to 2.8%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Ashford (2.7 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Ashford decreased by 2.7 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Ashford

In 2021, 5.8% of Ashford residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 3.4% in 2011. The 2.4 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South East, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 5.2% to 7.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 88.1% of people in Ashford identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 93.7% in 2011), while 2.6% identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category (compared with 1.2% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category increased from 1.4% in 2011 to 2.2% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 5.8% of usual residents in Ashford identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Religion in Ashford

In 2021, 40.7% of Ashford residents reported having "No religion", up from 26.3% in 2011. The rise of 14.4 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Ashford. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South East, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.7% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 47.6% of people in Ashford described themselves as Christian (down from 62.9%), while 5.7% did not state their religion (down from 7.6% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 40.7% of usual residents in Ashford reported having "No religion"

National identity in Ashford

In 2021, 7.4% of Ashford residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 5.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.7%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.6% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Ashford that identified as "British only" increased from 15.0% to 56.2%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK in Ashford (1.9 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the South East (1.6 percentage points, from 7.1% to 8.7%). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Ashford increased by 1.9 percentage points

Fewer couples without children

Of Ashford households, 17.5% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 19.8% in 2011.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in Ashford (2.3 percentage points) than across the South East (1.4 percentage points, from 18.7% to 17.4%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Ashford decreased by 2.3 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Ashford residents aged 16 years and over, 33.1% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 29.0% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (49.3%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 51.9% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Ashford that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership decreased from 9.5% to 9.4%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater in Ashford (4.1 percentage points) than across the South East (2.9 percentage points, from 31.9% to 34.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Ashford increased by 4.1 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Ashford residents aged 16 years and over, 58.3% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 59.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 40 people (2.4%) said they were unemployed, compared with 3.3% in 2011. The percentage of retired Ashford residents increased from 22.1% to 22.5%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in Ashford (1.6 percentage points) than across the South East (1.3 percentage points, from 59.0% to 57.6%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Ashford decreased by 1.6 percentage points

Working hours in Ashford

In 2021, 10.6% of Ashford residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure was at a similar level in 2011 (10.4%).

In 2021, just over one in eight people (13.1%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 15.3% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 55.1% to 57.7%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week increased from 10.4% to 11.0% across the South East. Across England, the percentage increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Ashford increased by 0.2 percentage points

Disability in Ashford

In 2021, 6.9% of Ashford residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 7.7% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 people (10.3%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.7% in 2011. The proportion of Ashford residents who were not disabled increased from 82.6% to 82.8%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Ashford (0.8 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (1.0 percentage points, from 7.2% to 6.2%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Ashford decreased by 0.8 percentage points

Health in Ashford

In 2021, 47.8% of Ashford residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 45.6% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 35.9% to 35.0%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Ashford residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.0% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" was 3.6% (similar to 2011).

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Ashford increased by 2.2 percentage points
